title: Tian de Légumes
subtitle: Provençal layered vegetable bake
excerpt: Courgette, tomatoes, and aubergine sliced into rounds, layered in a dish with garlic and thyme, drizzled with olive oil, and baked slowly until collapsed and caramelised at the edges. A beautiful, simple dish from Provence.
sourceNotes: A tian is both a Provençal earthenware dish with straight sides and the food baked in it. The vegetable tian, courgettes, tomatoes, and occasionally aubergine or potatoes, layered with garlic, thyme, and olive oil, is a classic of Provençal summer cooking. Richard Olney, Simple French Food (1974), describes the tian in the Provençal vegetables chapter. Elizabeth David, A Book of Mediterranean Food (1950), documents the dish. The word tian comes from the Greek teganon, 'frying pan', via the Latin teganum.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tian can be made 2 hours ahead and served at room temperature. It is also excellent the following day, cold or reheated.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Provençal earthenware baking dish with straight sides, and the food baked in it. The classic vegetable tian layers sliced summer vegetables with oil, garlic, and herbs and bakes them slowly. The word comes from Greek via Latin.

content.text: is Provençal summer food at its most direct. Courgettes, tomatoes, and aubergine are sliced thin, layered in a dish with garlic and thyme, and soaked with olive oil. They bake slowly until the vegetables have collapsed and the edges have browned into the oil. It is one of the best dishes to bring to the table, and almost entirely mechanical to prepare: slice, layer, bake.

items.prepNote: sliced into 5 mm rounds, or use a mix of colours

content.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Spread the sliced onions over the base of the gratin dish and scatter with half the garlic and half the thyme. Season and drizzle with 2 tbsp of the olive oil.

Arrange the vegetable rounds in overlapping rows on top of the onion base, alternating courgette, tomato, and aubergine in a pattern. Press them gently into the dish, they should be close together, standing upright on their edges.
Tuck the remaining garlic slices between the vegetable rounds. Scatter with the remaining thyme. Season well with salt and pepper. Pour the remaining 4 tbsp of olive oil evenly over the top.

Bake at 180°C fan for 45 to 60 minutes, pressing the vegetables gently halfway through, until they are completely tender and the exposed edges and top are caramelised. The tian should be significantly reduced in volume. Serve hot, warm, or at room temperature.

items.symptom: The vegetables are still firm after 60 minutes
items.cause: The slices were cut too thick, or the oven temperature was too low.
items.fix: Continue baking for a further 15 to 20 minutes. A tian is best when the vegetables are fully collapsed and soft, not al dente. The tomatoes especially need to break down completely.

items.symptom: The tian is watery at the bottom
items.cause: The tomatoes and courgettes have released their moisture.
items.fix: This is normal and the liquid is delicious. If it is excessive, return to the oven uncovered for a further 10 minutes to allow it to evaporate. A well-reduced tian will have absorbed most of this liquid by the end.

items.symptom: The top layer is drying out without browning underneath
items.cause: All the olive oil was poured on top rather than distributed through the layers.
items.fix: Ensure the onion base is well oiled and season the base as well as the top. The base vegetables cook by steaming in the bottom liquid; the top caramelises in the oil.

content.text: The tian is quintessentially Provençal. The earthenware dish of the same name was traditionally used for everything from gratins to rice bakes, and in summer the vegetable tian became one of the staple dishes of the Provençal table. The dish shares its DNA with ratatouille but is radically simpler: no preliminary frying of each vegetable, no separate cooking stages. The beauty is that the vegetables cook as one in the oven, absorbing the olive oil and each other's juices over the long bake.
